summary: Wilhelm Geiger was an Indology, Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, later serving as professor there (1891) and as professor at the University of Munich (1920-1924).

Wilhelm Grube worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Leipzig University, where he earned his PhD under Georg von der Gabelentz. He later held posts at the Ethnological Museum and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Wilhelm Gundert was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He succeeded Karl Florenz and held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1936 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen, later holding posts at Göttingen, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Pennsylvania (1982-2000).

Wilhelm Havers was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1915-1917), the University of Bern (~1917-1920), the University of Breslau (~1920-1929), the University of Würzburg (~1929-1937), and the University of Vienna (~1937-1953).

Wilhelm Max Müller was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883-1885) and Leipzig University (~1885-1888), and later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910-1919).

Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Tübingen under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as head and head librarian at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha.
Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Schulze from circa 1906 to 1911 and under Heinrich Lüders from circa 1909 to 1911.

Wilhelm Radloff worked in Central Asian studies, linguistics, and archaeology. Educated in Berlin and Jena, he was director of the Asiatic Museum (1885-1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (1894-1918).

Wilhelm Rau was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Leipzig and earned his doctorate at Marburg under Johannes Nobel, later serving as professor at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955) and Ordinarius at the University of Marburg (1958-1987).

Wilhelm Scherer was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna and in Berlin under Moriz Haupt and Franz Bopp. He held chairs at the University of Vienna, the University of Strasbourg, and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1877).

Wilhelm Schmidt was a linguist and religious studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893-1895). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1921-1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939-1951).

Wilhelm Schott was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1823 to 1826 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1838 to 1889.

Wilhelm Schulze was a linguist and Indologist. After studies in Berlin and Greifswald, he held posts at the University of Marburg and the University of Göttingen, before occupying a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1902 to 1932.
Wilhelm Schüler was a Sinologist who held a professorship at the Seminar for Oriental Languages in Berlin from circa 1913 to 1934.
Wilhelm Solf was an Indologist. He studied under Richard Pischel at Halle-Wittenberg and pursued studies in Berlin, Göttingen, Jena, and Kiel, where he also held a post from circa 1889 to 1890.
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp from circa 1850 to 1854 and under Moriz Haupt from circa 1853 to 1855.

Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Münster, Berlin, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann. He held professorships at the University of Fribourg, University of Münster, University of Munich, and Leipzig University (1920-1925).

Wilhelm Wackernagel was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He served as professor and Ordinarius at the University of Basel from 1833 until 1869.

Wilhelm Wundt was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (1857), Leipzig University (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).
